name: Герои Эхо недели людей — народ речных тростников, отбивший нашествие Ан-Кешара «Ночь, которую назвали звёзды» (ADR-0023, ADR-0024; docs/content/герои/состав-героев.md, «Люди — Ан-Кешар»; RS.weeks в design/ui/roster.js). Пятеро по герою за цикл II–VI: c2-50 Иру Тростниковый, c3-47 Лимту Илистая, c4-47 Ашнун Запруда, c5-55 Эннату Лучница Камыша, c6-47 Кидду Звездоборец. Задание 30.09.2026: портреты для окон призыва и Эхо вместо инициалов. Рецепт — принятый отряд Иш-Кантуна (jobs/heroes-echo-ishkantun.json): тот же стиль, запреты, три референса стиля, кадр по пояс, корпус вправо, к врагам, камера чуть снизу; каждый — по способу «Глубокий промт персонажа» (art/style/style.md): кто он и чего хочет сейчас · характер телом · поза словами в миг действия · пять личных деталей из «кто он» и глав (roster.js, ch) · место. Раса — Забытые: облик ни на кого из нынешних не похож, у каждого народа недели свой. Народ тростников — решение агента по главам: высокие, как цапли, кожа цвета мокрого ила, волосы, выгоревшие на концах, волнистые линии речной глины; тростник, кость, смола, обожжённая глина; год меряют водой. Враги недели — звездочёты Ан-Кешара (jobs/echo-ankeshar.json): бронза, синие жрецы, колесницы, знамёна с крылатыми львами — только трофеи и угроза за правым краем. Класс — по оружию и действию, школа — по цвету света. Детали, которых нет в «кто он» и главах, — решение агента, по строке в source
style: Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, heroic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.
negative: No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no glyphs, no cuneiform, no wedge-shaped marks, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture, no gems or badges of rank. No bodies, no skulls, no blood. Only one character in the foreground; a person has exactly two arms and two hands. Not stiff, not passive, not posing like a mannequin; no empty eyes. The hero is not one of the star-gazers: no beard curled into rows of ringlets, no conical bronze helmet, no blue robe on the hero.

heroes.frame:
Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A close, heroic half-body portrait from the waist or hips up, three-quarter view; no knees, no legs, no feet in the frame. The camera is a little below the hero's chest and looks slightly up, so the hero towers — a legend, not an extra. The hero's body is turned toward the right side of the picture, toward unseen enemies beyond the right edge, and the face is seen in three-quarter view looking to the right. The hero is caught at the peak of an action that shows who they are; the pose carries weight and intent. Head in the upper third, the face large, well lit and readable at small size, with a clear expression; the lower quarter may be darker because the card puts the name there. Rich atmospheric background that tells where the hero lived, with depth and soft focus, darker than the character. Light comes from below and from glowing crystals; rim light separates the figure from the background.

The hero belongs to the people of the river reeds — a forgotten people who lived long before all the peoples of today, in endless reed marshes and on the earthen dams of a great slow river, downstream from the stepped towers of An-Keshar. They look unlike any people living now: tall, long-limbed and light like herons, with long narrow faces, high cheekbones and large, calm eyes of pale grey-green, the colour of river water; their skin is a deep olive-brown with a faint silvery sheen, like wet river silt; their dark hair is bleached pale at the ends by sun and water and bound in a long knot with reed cord; they paint thin wavy lines of pale grey river clay across their shoulders, forearms and cheekbones, like ripples on water. They wear short wraps and kilts of woven reed fibre and undyed linen, capes of plaited reed and belts of twisted reed; ornaments of freshwater shell, fish bone and small river pearls; their tools are simple — reed, bone, black river pitch, fired clay and a little copper; their boats and their arched houses are bundles of tall reeds. They measure the year by the water, from the great flood to the low water. Their enemies were the star-gazers of An-Keshar — spearmen in bronze helmets and bronze scale, priests in robes of deep lapis blue who sang the names of the nights, light war chariots, banners with winged lions and small gold star rosettes, stepped towers of fired brick faced with blue glazed brick far away on the horizon; such things appear only as trophies or as the threat beyond the right edge.

jobs.title: Иру Тростниковый — Забытые, контроль (на контроль), Вода (c2-50, Эхо, эпическая)
jobs.source: roster.js c2-50: «Когда колесницы звездочётов Ан-Кешара вошли в болото, Иру опутал их тростниковыми сетями»; глава «Сети в тростнике»: сети из сырого тростника — сырой не рвётся, а тянется; колёса взяты по ступицу; жрецы в синем кричали про твёрдую землю; последнюю сеть держал руками. Решение агента: миг, когда сеть натягивается на колесе у правого края; обрывок синей жреческой ткани на плече; костяная игла для сетей в узле волос. jobs.subject: Subject: Iru of the Reeds, a man of the river reeds, a trapper who binds enemies, of the Water school. Who he is: all winter he wove nets of raw green reed — raw reed does not tear, it stretches. On the night the sky had named, the war chariots of An-Keshar drove into the marsh as if into a field, and his nets caught their wheels up to the hubs. Right now a chariot has plunged into his net, and he hauls it tight. Character: stubborn, silent and furious — a patient marsh-dweller whose quiet has turned into hatred; his jaw clenched, his lips drawn back from his teeth with effort, his pale grey-green eyes fixed hard on the chariot beyond the right edge. Pose, the moment of the haul: the camera is low; he stands in the dark marsh water, turned toward the right, his long body leaning back against the pull with all his weight. He has exactly two arms: his near hand grips the thick rope of the net at his hip and pulls it back; his far hand grips the rope further forward, the forearm corded with strain. The net of wet green reed stretches taut from his hands toward the right edge, where the bronze rim of one chariot wheel is caught in its mesh up to the hub; water sprays from the stretched cords, and swirls of blue light of the Water school run along them. Details that tell his story: (1) the net is woven of raw green reed, still dripping, its knots fat and heavy; (2) his palms are wound with strips of wet linen, and fresh reed cuts cross his forearms; (3) a bone netting needle is stuck through the knot of his hair; (4) a torn strip of lapis-blue cloth from a priest's robe is tied around his upper arm; (5) wavy lines of pale grey clay run across his shoulders and cheekbones like ripples. Place: the reed marsh at night under a sky dense with stars: reeds taller than a man, black water, a fallen banner with a winged lion half-sunk in the water behind him; far away, the dark silhouette of a stepped brick tower on the horizon. Blue light of the Water school glows up from the black water below; starlight glitters on the wet reeds.

jobs.title: Лимту Илистая — Забытые, лекарь, Вода (c3-47, Эхо, уникальная)
jobs.source: roster.js c3-47: «Лекарка речного народа: лечила илом и речной водой, пока бронза Ан-Кешара шла по дамбам»; главы «Ил на ранах» (у корней тростника ил холодный и чистый; раненых возили на плотах; к утру в иле по локоть), «Последняя дамба» (рану врагу промыла, простить не стала; у последней дамбы осталась с ранеными). Решение агента: горсть светящегося ила летит вправо, на раненых за краем; шест плота в дальней руке; бронзовая чешуйка доспеха Ан-Кешара на шнуре — от врага, которого вылечила и не простила. К выгрузке — art/generated/heroes/hero-c3-47-limtu__nb2.jpg → design/ui/assets/art/heroes/c3-47.jpg
jobs.subject: Subject: Limtu the Silt-Healer, a woman of the river reeds, a healer of the Water school. Who she is: silt heals better than any leaf if you know where to take it — cold and clean at the roots of the reeds, bitter by the dam. When the bronze of An-Keshar marched along the dams, the wounded were brought to her on rafts, and by morning she was in silt up to the elbows; she retreated from dam to dam with the wounded and did not leave them at the last one. Right now a raft of wounded has reached her, and she lifts a handful of cold healing silt. Character: stern, tireless and quietly unforgiving — she heals everyone and forgives no one; her brows drawn together, her mouth pressed tight, her eyes steady and practical. Pose, the moment of healing: the camera is low; she stands in the shallow water at the foot of an earthen dam, turned toward the right, leaning forward. She has exactly two arms: her near arm is thrust out toward the right, and from her cupped hand a mass of cold grey-blue silt glowing with blue light pours toward the wounded beyond the right edge, water streaming between her fingers; her far hand holds upright the long punting pole of a reed raft beside her. Blue light of the Water school spirals around her outstretched hand. Details that tell her story: (1) both her arms are coated in grey silt up to the elbows; (2) a pouch of wet silt wrapped in broad reed leaves hangs at her belt; (3) rolls of linen bandages are slung over one shoulder; (4) a single bronze scale torn from the armour of An-Keshar hangs from a cord at her belt — from an enemy she healed and did not forgive; (5) her hair is bound up with reed cord and one small river pearl. Place: the last dam at night: a long earthen dam overgrown with reeds, reed rafts with small oil lamps moored along it behind her, the dark water rising; far away, torches on the dams and the stepped towers of An-Keshar. Blue light glows up from the cold water below; a few stars reflect in it.

jobs.subject: Subject: Ashnun of the Dam, a man of the river reeds, a defender of the Earth school. Who he is: the keeper of the great dam of his people for forty floods — a dam is not a wall but an argument with the river, and he never lost it. When the star-gazers came, their chariots sank in the silt at his feet, and the bronze spears could not move him a single step; on the second night he raised every sluice gate and let the river take the bronze ranks. Right now the bronze spearmen of An-Keshar climb over their stuck chariots at him. Character: immovable, stubborn and weather-worn — a heavy calm older man who has argued with a river all his life; his jaw set like the dam itself, his heavy brows lowered, his eyes calm and fixed on the enemy beyond the right edge; grey streaks in his hair and short beard. Framing: a close half-body shot — from the top of his head down to his belt; his legs and feet are not in the picture at all, his head and shoulders fill the upper half. Pose, the moment of holding: the camera is low; he stands on the crest of the dam, huge and square, turned toward the right, his weight sunk low. He has exactly two arms: his near arm holds up a tall, heavy shield of bundled reeds bound with black pitch and rawhide, angled toward the right, and snapped bronze spear points are stuck in it; his far hand grips the thick wet rope of a wooden sluice gate beside him, ready to heave it up. Amber-orange light of the Earth school rises from cracks in the packed clay of the dam, and clods of earth jump up where the spears strike. Details that tell his story: (1) the shield bristles with broken bronze spear points; (2) his forearms and chest are streaked with dried grey silt; (3) the heavy wooden beam of the sluice gate with its rope and a stone counterweight stands beside him; (4) a long string of river pearls around his neck, one for each flood he kept; (5) a torn banner with a winged lion hangs from the sluice beam behind him. Place: the great dam at night: the dark river on one side, a wide low marshland on the other; beyond the right edge the glint of conical bronze helmets and raised spears; a sky full of stars. Amber light from the cracks in the dam below, cold starlight on the water.

jobs.subject: Subject: Ennatu Reed-Archer, a woman of the river reeds, a swift archer of the Air school. Who she is: she grew up in the reeds with a bow, as others grow up with an oar; her people shoot low, just above the water, so as not to scare the flock. On the night of the invasion she shot from the reeds at the voices of the singing priests in blue and at the poles of the star banners, and the banners fell into the water one after another. Right now a banner-bearer with a winged lion wades forward beyond the right edge, and she looses. Character: sharp, fierce and bright-eyed — a hunter who waits and never misses; her eyes narrowed, one corner of her mouth pulled into a grim half-smile, her whole body taut as the bowstring. Pose, the moment of the shot: the camera is low; she rises from the reeds, turned toward the right, her body low and coiled. She has exactly two arms: her near arm holds a long bow of reed and horn out toward the right, tilted almost level, just above the water; her far hand has just released the string beside her cheek, the fingers opening. The arrow skims away toward the right low over the black water, trailing a thin spiral of pale white-green wind that flattens the reeds and ruffles the water (Air). Details that tell her story: (1) a quiver of reed arrows fletched with grey heron feathers at her hip; (2) a small gold star rosette torn from an enemy banner is tied into her hair; (3) she wears nothing blue — only undyed linen and reed; (4) her face and arms are streaked with dark silt to hide in the reeds; (5) cut reed stalks for spare shafts are tucked in her belt. Place: the reed beds at night under a sky full of stars: tall dark reeds around her, black water, and beyond it, in soft focus, fallen banners with winged lions floating face down. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the water and the reeds below; stars reflect on the water.

jobs.subject: Subject: Kiddu Star-Fighter, a man of the river reeds, a battle mage of the Time school. Who he is: as a boy he was traded to a tower of An-Keshar for a boat of reeds, to carry water up to the priests on the highest step; there he learned to read the sky from scraps of their songs, and his count of the nights ran further than theirs. He read the night of the invasion before the priests did, and met them where their own sky pointed: he sang their song with his own count and led the bronze ranks into the lowland below the dam. Right now he turns their own stars against them. Character: brilliant, bitter and unforgiving — a cold certainty: he knows the sky better than those who taught it; his head lifted, his eyes reflecting the stars, his mouth open in a low chant. Pose, the moment of the spell: the camera is low; he stands on the dam at night, turned toward the right, his long body stretched tall. He has exactly two arms: his near arm is raised high toward the right, the finger pointing at one bright star; from that star a thin shaft of green light descends and spreads into a wide, slowly turning ring of green light over the enemy beyond the right edge (Time); his far hand holds at his chest a long cord of knotted reed strung with small river pebbles — his count of the nights. Green motes of light fall around him like slow sand. Details that tell his story: (1) an old clay water jar hangs on a cord across his back — the jar he carried up the tower as a boy; (2) the cord of knots and pebbles is very long and wound twice around his wrist; (3) his hair is grey at the temples and bound with reed cord; (4) thin wavy clay lines on his cheekbones; (5) a scrap of faded blue cloth is wound around the neck of the jar. Place: the dam above a flooded lowland at night under a vast sky crowded with stars; far away on the horizon, a dark stepped tower of brick with no fire at its top. Green light of the Time school glows up from the still water below, where the stars are reflected.
